inScope: This record, committed first on the focused branch feat/ent-240-readela-0.3.0 from baseCommit.

Preferences version 2 under the existing key: direction page/auto/rtl/ltr, theme page/paper/night, font page/sans, size and spacing unchanged; field-by-field migration from version 1 in which serif becomes page and every other stored choice is kept.
Direction as one independent reading aspect whose unchanged state leaves the page's own direction alone.

Reading appearance Paper and Night, chosen independently of the site's own theme and limited to the reading surface of responses; palette values fixed by a deterministic contrast calculation with primary reading text at 10:1 or better.

Readela Sans: the official unmodified Vazirmatn (Non-Latin, variable weight) bundled for Arabic-script text, with the SIL Open Font License 1.1 text and the upstream version, file and SHA-256 recorded; one web-accessible resource entry for that file, limited to the two supported hosts.
A reading mark per conversation: Mark here, Go to mark and Clear in the popup; stored locally as one-way fingerprints only; exact, approximate and not-found outcomes; no automatic scrolling.
Popup redesign with Readela as the heading, and the message exchange between the popup and the active tab that the reading mark needs, without a new permission.
Tests and documentation made necessary by the above; version 0.3.0; dated evidence under docs/evidence/.
A local unpacked Chrome build for owner visual review.
outOfScope: Submission or publication to the Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons, a GitHub Release or any other provider; a v0.3.0 tag.
Custom fonts, notes, durable highlighting, read aloud, focus mode, additional sites, Edge or Safari work.
A new permission, a broader match pattern, a backend, analytics, telemetry, remote code or any network request.
A general site recolouring engine, and any recolouring of site navigation, the composer or controls outside the reading surface.
Dependency changes, a new build system and unrelated refactors.
Changes to declared Capabilities or Exceptions, to the dev-standards pin and to the repository ruleset.

capabilities.assessment: The extension remains a browser interface with no backend or operated service, no data analysis and no new platform. Bundling a font and storing a local reading mark add no Capability.

items.capability: A font file packaged in the extension can be used by the content stylesheet on the two supported hosts in Chrome and Firefox.
items.authority: MDN web_accessible_resources (read 2026-10-10): web-accessible extension resources are not blocked by the page's CORS or CSP; Manifest V3 entries take resources and matches.
items.probe: The end-to-end suite asserts in real Chrome and Firefox that Arabic-script text is rendered with the bundled face.

items.capability: An extension page can query the active tab and send a message to the content script in it without the tabs permission.
items.authority: Chrome tabs API reference (read 2026-10-10): most features need no permission; only url, pendingUrl, title and favIconUrl are gated.
items.probe: The end-to-end suite operates the reading mark from the installed popup in real Chrome and Firefox; the manifest test keeps permissions at ["storage"].

items.capability: The page structure of the two supported sites that the reading surface and the reading mark rely on.
items.authority: Read-only structural observation of signed-in conversation pages in the owner's browser on 2026-10-10 (element names, attribute names and computed colours only; no conversation text recorded).
items.probe: Recorded in the dated evidence; the design fails safe to the site's own presentation where a structure is not recognised.
